mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 9% triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as high unemployment indicates a weakening economy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 9%, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and GDP (GDPC1) both increase, it signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal from HOUST and GDPC1 does not outperform a random walk in predicting 60-day forward returns, or the signal's Sharpe ratio is below 0.5 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, indicating supply chain disruptions.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 40% of instances when INDPRO falls below its 6-month MA, or the signal's information coefficient is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The spread between the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals the monetary policy stance, with a negative spread indicating an accommodative policy and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The spread between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not predict 5-day forward returns, or the signal's Sortino ratio is below 0.5 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 3-month moving average triggers a positive signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, indicating a strong labor market.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 30% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds its 3-month MA, or the signal's hit ratio is below 0.6 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of increasing retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal from RSAFS and HOUST does not outperform a random walk in predicting 60-day forward returns, or the signal's Calmar ratio is below 0.5 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) jointly signal a supply chain stress regime, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal from INDPRO and UNRATE does not predict 20-day forward returns, or the signal's information coefficient is below 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.
